### 2026-11-08: # Coded some nice and juicy firmwaree!

**2.45h**

# Coded some nice and juicy firmwaree!

So for this session I decided to code some firmware for the macropad. But first I had to learn what to do.

First things first: what libraries?

I decided to go with kmk (circuitpython). I did some research on it, and learned the basics of circuitpython. It was kinda similar to micropython, but some differences gave me some difficulties. Eventually, I learned.

After that I decided to install the extension for vscode:

![Screenshot_20261108_175136](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/hld3Z4tOOA3MrvpstF1av8eSaMvDNCLn/8b9918887bc14820a2848d5afda540d94ed5c9131d39c52d0460f320a515e797.png)

_The extension docs_

But that didn't work as I expected, so instead, I installed the circuitpython-stubs using a venv and pip.

With that ready, I had to install kmk. That wasn't hard lol. What came next was the hard part.

I thought I knew enough about keyboard matrices, but I was wrong. The first challenge was choosing whether my board setup was row2col or col2row. To guide me, I used this amazing [guide](https://komar.blog/posts/how-to-make-a-keyboard-the-matrix/).

![Screenshot_20261108_201107](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/hld3Z4tOOA3MrvpstF1av8eSaMvDNCLn/84991322aadb7c4f28976ee1341db8b3f891b1929b11b5f62e4b317f80baf954.png)

_The guide_

I learned a lot from there and finally understood how the diodes stopped ghosting from happening. But I think that was too much info for my brain, so I decided to take a break and go to the grocery store with my family.

1.5h later, I came back to finish the firmware. I guided myself through the kmk starter code and eventually understood it (took longer than I want to admit lol). In the end, I had my matrix fully configured.

Next I decided to add some layers to the macropad. I had to follow [kmk's guide](https://github.com/KMKfw/kmk_firmware/blob/main/docs/en/layers.md) on layers, and eventually got it working.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/hld3Z4tOOA3MrvpstF1av8eSaMvDNCLn/3a0a0edc5c4840bdcb637c4c8284794b138a139cf509764eb3f099c238cc008b.png)

_Kmk's guide_

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/hld3Z4tOOA3MrvpstF1av8eSaMvDNCLn/800a73cd237699237775589457d19b2b8ffe1468ea83fea0b25dad1339321985.png)

_My layout_

I added 4 layouts to have plenty of options. I already assigned 2, and have 2 more in case I want to add new keybinds in the future.

Then was time to set up the rotary encoder. At first, I tried to configure it using circuitpython's native libraries, but asking Gemini about the situation revealed that I could just use the built-in [encoder module](https://github.com/KMKfw/kmk_firmware/blob/main/docs/en/encoder.md), so that's what I did!

I began by reading the docs and configuring my encoder's pins. It took me longer than I'd like to admit to understand the docs lol.

![Screenshot_20261108_214113](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/hld3Z4tOOA3MrvpstF1av8eSaMvDNCLn/510f6ef7211d64edd767f7fe1f2b40ffc10e7a08ded7344e2c050d9d9916397c.png)

_The documentation page_

Something that confused me a bit was the part where I had to set up the encoder pins, and **then** set up the layout. I thought I had to do both at the same time, and I lost quite some time doing that lol.

Finally I decided to add some LEDs to signal the active layer. For that, I edited the built-in [statusled extension](https://github.com/KMKfw/kmk_firmware/blob/main/docs/en/extension_statusled.md) to make it work with 4 LEDs. It was a very minor edit, but I had a hard time reading some of the code because I was new to circuitpython.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/hld3Z4tOOA3MrvpstF1av8eSaMvDNCLn/241961016bd87b5635ce3bd279d43696f69d98f91bbc859f303a61c1ff7defe0.png)

_The edit_

I haven't yet hooked up the logic here because I'm yet to add the LEDs to the PCB. Also, I haven't added the long-press-to-switch-layers feature to the rotary encoder, but that's a problem for the next lapse entry!

In the end, I spent probably 50% learning and 50% coding. You can check the hackatime entry for this session.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/hld3Z4tOOA3MrvpstF1av8eSaMvDNCLn/f4f5f79df93199b350000633326151b95d7c6682b23b5bfaab826b03cff48a5e.png)

_Hackatime_

And that was it! I learned a lot and enjoyed this! I hope I can finish the macropad soon because I really want to use it daily!
